claim: Integrins are transmembrane receptors composed of α and β subunits.
source: Integrins are transmembrane receptors composed of α and β subunits.
evidence: This is a foundational statement about integrin structure that is established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Most integrins contain β1.
source: Although most integrins contain β1, canonical activation mechanisms are based on studies of the platelet integrin, αIIbβ3.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about the prevalence of β1-containing integrins.

claim: Canonical activation mechanisms are based on studies of the platelet integrin, αIIbβ3.
source: Although most integrins contain β1, canonical activation mechanisms are based on studies of the platelet integrin, αIIbβ3.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical basis of integrin activation models in the field.

claim: The inactive conformation of αIIbβ3 is characterized by the association of the αIIb transmembrane and cytosolic domain (TM/CT) with a tilted β3 TM/CT.
source: Its inactive conformation is characterized by the association of the αIIb transmembrane and cytosolic domain (TM/CT) with a tilted β3 TM/CT that leads to activation when disrupted.
evidence: This describes the established structural model for inactive αIIbβ3 integrin.

claim: There are significant structural differences between β1 and β3 TM/CT in bicelles.
source: We show significant structural differences between β1 and β3 TM/CT in bicelles.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by NMR structural data presented in Figure 2.

claim: The 'snorkeling' lysine at the TM/CT interface of β subunits was previously proposed to regulate αIIbβ3 activation by ion pairing with nearby lipids.
source: Moreover, the 'snorkeling' lysine at the TM/CT interface of β subunits, previously proposed to regulate αIIbβ3 activation by ion pairing with nearby lipids, plays opposite roles in β1 and β3 integrin function and in neither case is responsible for TM tilt.
evidence: This references prior work proposing the snorkeling mechanism.

claim: The 'snorkeling' lysine plays opposite roles in β1 and β3 integrin function.
source: Moreover, the 'snorkeling' lysine at the TM/CT interface of β subunits, previously proposed to regulate αIIbβ3 activation by ion pairing with nearby lipids, plays opposite roles in β1 and β3 integrin function and in neither case is responsible for TM tilt.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cell adhesion and spreading data in Figure 1.

claim: The 'snorkeling' lysine is not responsible for TM tilt in either β1 or β3.
source: Moreover, the 'snorkeling' lysine at the TM/CT interface of β subunits, previously proposed to regulate αIIbβ3 activation by ion pairing with nearby lipids, plays opposite roles in β1 and β3 integrin function and in neither case is responsible for TM tilt.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by paramagnetic probe NMR data in Figures 3-5.

claim: A range of affinities from almost no interaction to relatively high avidity exists between various α subunits and β1 TM/CTs.
source: A range of affinities from almost no interaction to the relatively high avidity that characterizes αIIbβ3 is seen between various α subunits and β1 TM/CTs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by NMR and fluorescence anisotropy binding data in Figures 6-7 and Table 1.

claim: The αIIbβ3-based canonical model for the roles of the TM/CT in integrin activation and function does not extend to all mammalian integrins.
source: The αIIbβ3-based canonical model for the roles of the TM/CT in integrin activation and function clearly does not extend to all mammalian integrins.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, inferred from the collective experimental data showing differences between β1 and β3 integrins.

claim: The 18 α and 8 β integrin subunits associate non-covalently to form 24 heterodimeric integrins.
source: The 18 α and 8 β integrin subunits associate non-covalently to form 24 heterodimeric integrins, which are expressed in different combinations on all cell types throughout the body.
evidence: This is established knowledge about integrin diversity, supported by citations (Hynes, 2002; Mathew et al., 2012a; Pozzi and Zent, 2013).

claim: All integrin subunits, except β4, have a large extracellular ligand-binding domain, a single transmembrane domain (TM) that spans the cell membrane and a short cytosolic C-terminal domain (CT).
source: All integrin subunits, except β4, have a large extracellular ligand-binding domain, a single transmembrane domain (TM) that spans the cell membrane and a short cytosolic C-terminal domain (CT) that regulates integrin function by binding with cytoskeletal and signaling proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about integrin structure.

claim: β1 integrins are the principal integrins found in solid organs.
source: β1 integrins, in which the β1 subunit can be paired with any one of 12 different α isoforms, are the principal integrins found in solid organs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the tissue distribution of β1 integrins.

claim: The β1 subunit can be paired with any one of 12 different α isoforms.
source: β1 integrins, in which the β1 subunit can be paired with any one of 12 different α isoforms, are the principal integrins found in solid organs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about β1 integrin pairing possibilities.

claim: Integrin αIIbβ3 is found in the inactive state under normal conditions and activated to mediate platelet adhesion to fibrinogen following injury.
source: The paradigm for regulation of integrin affinity is set by the platelet-specific integrin αIIbβ3 found in the inactive state under normal conditions and activated to mediate platelet adhesion to fibrinogen following injury (Xiao et al., 2004) (Coller and Shattil, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about αIIbβ3 function, supported by citations.

claim: In the low affinity 'inactive' state integrin αIIbβ3 has a bent conformation that is stabilized by an outer clasp involving contacts between αIIb and β3 located near the middle and ectoplasmic ends of their TMs and an inner clasp involving αIIb/β3 contacts located in the cytosolic juxtamembrane domains.
source: In the low affinity 'inactive' state integrin αIIbβ3 has a bent conformation that is stabilized by an outer clasp involving contacts between αIIb and β3 located near the middle and ectoplasmic ends of their TMs and an inner clasp involving αIIb/β3 contacts located in the cytosolic juxtamembrane domains, the latter of which includes a critical salt bridge.
evidence: This describes the established structural model for inactive αIIbβ3, supported by citations (Lau et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2009; Zhu et al., 2009).

claim: Within the inactive state heterodimer, the αIIb transmembrane helix is thought to be reasonably well-aligned with the bilayer, while the long TM helix of β3 is thought to have a pronounced (25°) tilt angle.
source: Within the inactive state heterodimer, the αIIb transmembrane helix is thought be reasonably well-aligned with the bilayer, while the long TM helix of β3 is thought to have a pronounced (25°) tilt angle that is required to maintain simultaneous formation of the outer and inner clasps (Lau et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2009; Zhu et al., 2009).
evidence: This describes the established model for TM helix orientation in inactive αIIbβ3, supported by citations.

claim: It has been proposed that the tilt of the β3 TM in the inactive state is promoted by a 'snorkeling' interaction of the side chain ε-NH3+ moiety of the membrane-buried lysine-716 with a negatively charged lipid phosphodiester group located at the adjacent membrane-water interface.
source: It has been proposed that the tilt of the β3 TM in the inactive state is promoted by a 'snorkeling' interaction of the side chain ε-NH3+ moiety of the membrane-buried lysine-716 with a negatively charged lipid phosphodiester group located at the adjacent membrane-water interface (Kim et al., 2012).
evidence: This references a prior hypothesis about the mechanism of TM tilt, supported by citation.

claim: Following platelet activation, integrin αIIbβ3 is converted to a high affinity state that is mediated by the binding of intracellular cytoplasmic proteins to the CT of β3.
source: Following platelet activation, integrin αIIbβ3 is converted to a high affinity state that is mediated by the binding of intracellular cytoplasmic proteins to the CT of β3.
evidence: This is established knowledge about integrin activation mechanisms.

claim: Talin is a key regulator of integrin activation.
source: Talin is a key regulator of integrin activation and is comprised of head and rod domains.
evidence: This is established knowledge about talin's role in integrin regulation.

claim: Talin is comprised of head and rod domains.
source: Talin is a key regulator of integrin activation and is comprised of head and rod domains.
evidence: This is established knowledge about talin structure.

claim: The talin head has an atypical FERM domain containing four subdomains: F0-F3.
source: The head has an atypical FERM (band 4.1, ezrin, radixin, and moesin) domain containing four subdomains: F0-F3.
evidence: This is established knowledge about talin structure.

claim: The F3 subdomain of talin contains a phosphotyrosine-binding (PTB) signature that binds to the NPxY motif shared by both integrin β1 and β3 CT.
source: F3 contains a phosphotyrosine-binding (PTB) signature that binds to the NPxY motif shared by both integrin β1 and β3 CT, while F0-F2 enhances binding through favorable electrostatic interactions with anionic lipids in the vicinity of the integrin on the membrane surface (Moore et al., 2012; Saltel et al., 2009; Anthis et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about talin-integrin interactions, supported by citations.

claim: Talin F0-F2 enhances binding through favorable electrostatic interactions with anionic lipids in the vicinity of the integrin on the membrane surface.
source: F3 contains a phosphotyrosine-binding (PTB) signature that binds to the NPxY motif shared by both integrin β1 and β3 CT, while F0-F2 enhances binding through favorable electrostatic interactions with anionic lipids in the vicinity of the integrin on the membrane surface (Moore et al., 2012; Saltel et al., 2009; Anthis et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about talin-membrane interactions, supported by citations.

claim: Talin binding leads to a reduction of the tilt angle of the β3 TM and destabilization of the inner membrane clasp between the β3 and αIIb subunits, promoting dissociation of the transmembrane domains and integrin activation.
source: This leads to a reduction of the tilt angle of the β3 TM and destabilization of the inner membrane clasp between the β3 and αIIb subunits, promoting dissociation of the transmembrane domains and integrin activation (Ye et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the established mechanism of talin-mediated integrin activation, supported by citation.

claim: There is evidence that the fibronectin α5β1 integrin may resemble αIIbβ3.
source: While there is evidence that the fibronectin α5β1 integrin may resemble αIIbβ3 (Takagi et al., 2003; Luo et al., 2004), it is unclear whether all the 12 possible αβ1 integrin combinations are activated similarly to αIIbβ3, or whether there is mechanistic heterogeneity underlying their various adhesive functions.
evidence: This references prior evidence suggesting similarity between α5β1 and αIIbβ3, supported by citations.

claim: It is unclear whether all the 12 possible αβ1 integrin combinations are activated similarly to αIIbβ3.
source: While there is evidence that the fibronectin α5β1 integrin may resemble αIIbβ3 (Takagi et al., 2003; Luo et al., 2004), it is unclear whether all the 12 possible αβ1 integrin combinations are activated similarly to αIIbβ3, or whether there is mechanistic heterogeneity underlying their various adhesive functions.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: The putative snorkeling lysine K752 of β1 integrin was shown to regulate activation of integrin α5β1 in the same manner as proposed for K716 of β3.
source: In addition, the putative snorkeling lysine K752 of β1 integrin was shown to regulate activation of integrin α5β1 in the same manner as proposed for K716 of β3 (Kim et al., 2012).
evidence: This references prior work on β1 K752, supported by citation.

claim: Disruption of the inner membrane clasp in β1 integrin did not cause any phenotype in knockin mice.
source: By contrast, disruption of the inner membrane clasp in β1 integrin did not cause any phenotype in knockin mice, nor did it alter integrin activation as assessed by activation-dependent antibodies or cell adhesion and migration on fibronectin (Czuchra et al., 2006).
evidence: This references prior experimental findings, supported by citation.

claim: Disruption of the inner membrane clasp in β1 integrin did not alter integrin activation as assessed by activation-dependent antibodies or cell adhesion and migration on fibronectin.
source: By contrast, disruption of the inner membrane clasp in β1 integrin did not cause any phenotype in knockin mice, nor did it alter integrin activation as assessed by activation-dependent antibodies or cell adhesion and migration on fibronectin (Czuchra et al., 2006).
evidence: This references prior experimental findings, supported by citation.

claim: Ligand (i.e. collagen) binding to the integrins α1β1 and α2β1 has been reported to occur in the absence of integrin activation.
source: Moreover, contrary to the canonical model, ligand (i.e. collagen) binding to the integrins α1β1 and α2β1 has been reported to occur in the absence of integrin activation (Abair et al., 2008a; Nissinen et al., 2012).
evidence: This references prior findings that challenge the canonical model, supported by citations.

claim: The β1-K752R mutation did not significantly change CD cell adhesion to collagen I.
source: The β1-K752R mutation (which maintained the positive amino acid charge) did not significantly change CD cell adhesion to collagen I (0.5 μg/ml) in the absence or presence of an integrin α1 blocking antibody (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: CD cells expressing the β1-K752E mutation exhibited little adhesion to collagen I.
source: However, under the same conditions, CD cells expressing the β1-K752E mutation (which changed the amino acid charge from positive to negative) exhibited little adhesion to collagen I in the absence or presence of an integrin α1 blocking antibody (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: CD cells expressing the β1-K752E mutation spread significantly less on collagen I than CD cells expressing wild type β1 integrin at 15, 30 and 45 min.
source: CD cells expressing the β1-K752E mutation spread significantly less on collagen I than CD cells expressing wild type β1 integrin at 15, 30 and 45 min (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: The intensity of 12G10/AIIB2 antibody binding was significantly less in the β1-K752E mutant compared to WT CD cells.
source: The intensity of 12G10/AIIB2 antibody binding was significantly less in the β1-K752E mutant compared to WT CD cells.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1G and H.

claim: The difference in 12G10/AIIB2 antibody binding between β1-K752E mutant and WT was no longer present when the cells were adhered in the presence of Mn2+.
source: This difference was no longer present when the cells were adhered in the presence of Mn2+, which is known to artificially activate integrins (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1G and H.

claim: Reversing the basic charge of the snorkeling lysine near the TM domain of the β1 integrin significantly decreased integrin α1β1 and α2β1-dependent adhesion to and spreading on collagens by polarized CD epithelial cells.
source: Thus, reversing the basic charge of the snorkeling lysine near the TM domain of the β1 integrin significantly decreased integrin α1β1 and α2β1-dependent adhesion to and spreading on collagens by polarized CD epithelial cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: The β1-K752E mutation resulted in a lower affinity state of β1 integrin in the context of CD cells adherent on collagen I.
source: In addition, it resulted in a lower affinity state of β1 integrin in the context of CD cells adherent on collagen I.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 12G10 antibody binding data in Figure 1G and H.

claim: For β1, there is an α-helix extending from the N-terminal I732 at the beginning of the TM to K765 located in the cytosol, roughly eight sites beyond the end of the TM.
source: For β1, there is an α-helix extending from the N-terminal I732 at the beginning of the TM to K765 located in the cytosol, roughly eight sites beyond the end of the TM.
evidence: This is a primary structural finding based on NMR chemical shift analysis shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: For the β3 TM/CT, the helix starts at the beginning of the TM (at I693), but extends roughly 16 residues into the cytosol, terminating only at A737.
source: For the β3 TM/CT, this helix also starts at the beginning of the TM (at I693), but extends roughly 16 residues into the cytosol, terminating only at A737.
evidence: This is a primary structural finding based on NMR chemical shift analysis shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Beyond the TM/CT helix, the remaining intracellular domains of both integrin β1 and integrin β3 are unstructured.
source: Beyond the TM/CT helix, the remaining intracellular domains of both integrin β1 and integrin β3 are unstructured.
evidence: This is a primary structural finding based on NMR chemical shift analysis shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The degree to which the TM helix of the β3 integrin extends further into the CT relative to β1 (nine residues longer for β3) is striking.
source: The degree to which the TM helix of the β3 integrin extends further into the CT relative to β1 (nine residues longer for β3) is striking.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data comparing β1 and β3.

claim: The transmembrane helix is rigid and exchange-resistant.
source: Results from these experiments (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2) show that the transmembrane helix is rigid and, not surprisingly, exchange-resistant.
evidence: This is a finding based on hydrogen exchange and relaxation NMR data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The CT segments identified as helical by analysis of the chemical shifts exhibit a gradient of low exchange/low motion to significantly higher exchange and motion going from the end of the TM to the end of the chemical-shift identified CT helical segments.
source: The CT segments identified as helical by analysis of the chemical shifts are seen to exhibit a gradient of low exchange/low motion to significantly higher exchange and motion going from the end of the TM to the end of the chemical-shift identified CT helical segments.
evidence: This is a finding based on hydrogen exchange and relaxation NMR data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: There is a modest spike in exchange and motion observed at the TM/CT interface.
source: There is also a modest spike in exchange and motion observed at the TM/CT interface.
evidence: This is a finding based on hydrogen exchange and relaxation NMR data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The CT helix is extended away from the membrane into the cytosol.
source: It is very clear from the topological analysis presented in the following sections that the CT helix is extended away from the membrane into the cytosol and that any hinge motions at the TM/CT interface are not of sufficient magnitude to enable significant interactions of the CT helix with the membrane surface.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the paramagnetic probe accessibility data presented in subsequent figures.

claim: The beginning and ends of the β1 TM are near sites I732 and I757, respectively.
source: The plateau in peak ratios observed when Gd(III)-DTPA was used, combined with the corresponding trough in the ratio when 16-DSA was used indicates that the beginning and ends of the TM are near sites I732 and I757, respectively.
evidence: This is a finding based on paramagnetic probe accessibility NMR data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Both the extracellular segment and the cytosolic domains of β1 are largely exposed to the hydrophilic Gd(III)-DTPA.
source: Both the extracellular segment and the cytosolic domains are largely exposed to the hydrophilic Gd(III)-DTPA (Figure 3A and C), although the modest degree of protection to Gd(III)-DTPA near the P781IY segment (see spike in right side of Figure 3C) suggests that this segment undergoes transient interactions with the bicelle surface.
evidence: This is a finding based on paramagnetic probe accessibility NMR data shown in Figure 3A and C.

claim: The β1 TM includes both the putative 'snorkeling' Lys site (752 in β1, 716 in β3) and the five hydrophobic residues following it.
source: Importantly, these results show that, similar to integrin β3, the β1 TM includes both the putative 'snorkeling' Lys site (752 in β1, 716 in β3) and the five hydrophobic residues following it.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the paramagnetic probe accessibility data in Figure 3.

claim: The β1 TM is terminated by the HDRRE762 motif, where D759 corresponds to D723 in β3.
source: The β1 TM is terminated by the HDRRE762 motif, where D759 corresponds to D723 in β3, which forms a critical salt bridge with R995 in the αIIb subunit as part of the 'inner clasp' that stabilizes the inactive integrin heterodimeric state (Lau et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the paramagnetic probe accessibility data in Figure 3, combined with knowledge from prior work cited.

claim: Both β1-K752E and β1-K752R mutants yielded almost exactly the same patterns of accessibility to both paramagnetic probes as WT β1.
source: Surprisingly, both mutants yielded almost exactly the same patterns of accessibility to both paramagnetic probes as WT (Figure 3A and C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), indicating that both charge-conservative and charge reversal mutations at K752 induce little change in the membrane topology or tilt of the TM helix of β1 TM/CT.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on paramagnetic probe accessibility NMR data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both charge-conservative and charge reversal mutations at K752 induce little change in the membrane topology or tilt of the TM helix of β1 TM/CT.
source: Surprisingly, both mutants yielded almost exactly the same patterns of accessibility to both paramagnetic probes as WT (Figure 3A and C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), indicating that both charge-conservative and charge reversal mutations at K752 induce little change in the membrane topology or tilt of the TM helix of β1 TM/CT.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the paramagnetic probe accessibility NMR data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A previous study presented Mn(II)-EDDA probe accessibility data showing that the β3-K716E mutation induced a major change in membrane topology for the isolated integrin β3 TM.
source: The fact that the β1-K752E mutation did not impact the membrane topology/tilt for the β1 subunit was surprising in light of a previous study that presented Mn(II)-EDDA (polar) probe accessibility data showing that the β3-K716E mutation induced a major change in membrane topology, at least for the isolated integrin β3 TM (Kim et al., 2012).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: The authors' β3-WT vs. β3-K716E results using Mn(II)-EDDA are very similar to the previously reported results.
source: As shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, our β3-WT vs. β3-K716E results are very similar to the previously reported results.
evidence: This is a finding based on replication of prior experiments, shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Use of the hydrophilic Gd-DTPA probe led to a similar result as for Mn-EDDA for β3-WT vs. β3-K716E.
source: Use of the hydrophilic Gd-DTPA probe led to a similar result as for Mn-EDDA (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), yielding results consistent with a major change in tilt for the TM domain due to the β3-K716E mutation.
evidence: This is a finding based on paramagnetic probe accessibility NMR data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: For 16-DSA, little difference was observed between the membrane topology and tilt of β3-WT and the β3-K716E mutant.
source: However, a discordant result was obtained when the lipophilic 16-DSA was used as the paramagnetic probe (note that an apolar probe was not employed in the previous study (Kim et al., 2012) of the isolated β3 TM): for 16-DSA, little difference was observed between the membrane topology and tilt of β3-WT and the β3-K716E mutant (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on paramagnetic probe accessibility NMR data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Chelate probes such as Mn(II)-EDDA and Gd(III)-DTPA sometimes have an exposed ligand site that can transiently associate with anions such as Glu and Asp side chain carboxylates.
source: This led us to recall literature showing that chelate probes such as Mn(II)-EDDA and Gd(III)-DTPA sometimes have an exposed ligand site that can transiently associate with anions such as Glu and Asp side chain carboxylates (Hocking et al., 2013).
evidence: This references prior literature about chelate probe behavior, supported by citation.

claim: When excess EDTA was added to cap any free ligand sites in Gd(III)-DTPA, the β3-WT and β3-K716E mutant exhibited the same probe accessibility patterns.
source: Under these conditions the β3-WT and β3-K716E mutant exhibited the same probe accessibility patterns (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), fully consistent with the 16-DSA results.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on paramagnetic probe accessibility NMR data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The previously reported differences seen for the isolated β3 TM using Mn(II)-EDDA reflected an experimental artifact based on the tendency of free carboxyl groups in proteins to transiently serve as ligands to available metal ion coordination sites in chelate complexes.
source: These results indicate that the previously reported differences seen for the isolated β3 TM using Mn(II)-EDDA reflected an experimental artifact based on the tendency of free carboxyl groups in proteins (i.e., the introduced Glu716 side chain carboxyl) to transiently serve as ligands to available metal ion coordination sites in chelate complexes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data in Figure 4, explaining the discrepancy with prior work.

claim: The similarity of the membrane topology/tilt of β3-WT vs. β3-K716E is maintained when the full cytosolic domain is included (TM/CT).
source: We used both additional paramagnetic probe experiments and backbone amide 15N NMR R2 relaxation rate measurements to confirm that the similarity of the membrane topology/tilt of β3-WT vs. β3-K716E is maintained when the full cytosolic domain is included (TM/CT, Figure 5A–5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding based on paramagnetic probe accessibility and relaxation NMR data shown in Figure 5A–5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The membrane topology/tilt results for β3 were not altered by major changes in bicelle or buffer composition, pH, or temperature.
source: We also verified that these results were not altered by major changes in bicelle or buffer composition, pH, or temperature (Figure 5A and B vs. 5C and 5D, also Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding based on paramagnetic probe accessibility NMR data under different conditions shown in Figure 5.

claim: Membrane tilt/topology for both β1-WT and β1-K752E TM/CT does not strongly depend on lipid composition, buffer type, pH, or temperature.
source: Finally, the data of Figure 5E and F and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3 complements that of Figure 3C and D by showing that membrane tilt/topology for both β1-WT and β1-K752E TM/CT does not strongly depend on lipid composition, buffer type, pH, or temperature.
evidence: This is a finding based on paramagnetic probe accessibility NMR data under different conditions shown in Figure 5E and F and supplementary figures.

claim: For both the β1 and β3 integrins, the lysine buried in the membrane at the membrane/cytosol interface does not play a major role in dictating its TM topology or tilt, at least not for the free β subunits.
source: These results indicate that for both the β1 and β3 integrins, the lysine buried in the membrane at the membrane/cytosol interface does not play a major role in dictating its TM topology or tilt, at least not for the free β subunits.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the collective paramagnetic probe accessibility data in Figures 3-5.

claim: The β3-K716E mutation results in constitutive activation of the αIIbβ3 integrin and α5β1 integrins.
source: The β3-K716E mutation results in constitutive activation of the αIIbβ3 integrin and α5β1 integrins (Kim et al., 2012).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: Binding of integrin α5 to either the WT or K752E β1 TM/CT and binding of integrin αIIb to either WT or K716E β3 resulted in the disappearance of the β subunit TROSY NMR peaks rather than shifts, indicating 'slow exchange' between free and complexed subunits on the NMR time scale.
source: Binding of integrin α5 to either the WT or K752E β1 TM/CT and binding of integrin αIIb to either WT or K716E β3 resulted in the disappearance of the β subunit TROSY NMR peaks rather than shifts, indicating 'slow exchange' between free and complexed subunits on the NMR time scale (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR titration data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The αIIb TM/CT forms a relatively avid complex with the β3 TM/CT (Kd of ca. 0.1 mol%).
source: The binding results of Table 1 show that, as expected, the αIIb TM/CT forms a relatively avid complex with the β3 TM/CT (Kd of ca. 0.1 mol%) (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR and fluorescence anisotropy binding data shown in Table 1.

claim: The β3-K716E mutation reduced the affinity of the αIIbβ3 complex by roughly 4-fold (to a Kd of ca. 0.4 mol%).
source: Also as expected, the β3-K716E mutation reduced the affinity of this complex by roughly 4-fold (to a Kd of ca. 0.4 mol%).
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR and fluorescence anisotropy binding data shown in Table 1.

claim: Binding of WT α5 TM/CT to β1 TM/CT was avid (Kd of ca. 0.1 mol%).
source: Binding of WT α5 TM/CT to β1 TM/CT was also seen to be avid (Kd of ca. 0.1 mol%) (Table 1), while the K752E mutation in the β1 TM/CT reduces its binding affinity for α5 by a factor of 7 (Kd of ca. 0.7 mol%).
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR and fluorescence anisotropy binding data shown in Table 1.

claim: The K752E mutation in the β1 TM/CT reduces its binding affinity for α5 by a factor of 7 (Kd of ca. 0.7 mol%).
source: Binding of WT α5 TM/CT to β1 TM/CT was also seen to be avid (Kd of ca. 0.1 mol%) (Table 1), while the K752E mutation in the β1 TM/CT reduces its binding affinity for α5 by a factor of 7 (Kd of ca. 0.7 mol%).
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR and fluorescence anisotropy binding data shown in Table 1.

claim: This is consistent with a previous study that showed the β1-K752E mutation induces constitutive activation of the α5β1 integrin.
source: This is consistent with a previous study that showed the β1-K752E mutation induces constitutive activation of the α5β1 integrin (Kim et al., 2012).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: For all 4 combinations of α/β association of β1-WT and β1-K752E TM/CT with the α1 and α2 TM/CT, binding was so weak it could in no case be quantitated (Kd > 3.2 mol% for both α1β1 and α2β1 TM/CT).
source: It was very surprising that for all 4 combinations of α/β association of β1-WT and β1-K752E TM/CT with the α1 and α2 TM/CT that binding was so weak it could in no case be quantitated (Kd > 3.2 mol% for both α1β1 and α2β1 TM/CT) (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR and fluorescence anisotropy binding data shown in Table 1.

claim: The TM-K>E mutation decreases the affinity of the αβ heterodimers of both αIIbβ3 and α5β1 resulting in increased 'activity' of these integrins.
source: Together these data suggest that the TM-K>E mutation decreases the affinity of the αβ heterodimers of both αIIbβ3 and α5β1 resulting in increased 'activity' of these integrins.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the binding data in Table 1 and prior knowledge about integrin activation.

claim: Full length α1β1 and α2β1 integrins may be 'constitutively active' under physiological conditions and cannot be further activated.
source: These results also suggest that full length α1β1 and α2β1 integrins may be 'constitutively active' under physiological conditions and cannot be further activated.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the weak binding observed for α1β1 and α2β1 TM/CT in Table 1.

claim: Both the wild type and β1K752E CD cells adhered equally to fibronectin (0.5 μg/ml).
source: Both the wild type and β1K752E CD cells adhered equally to fibronectin (0.5 μg/ml) (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a finding based on cell adhesion data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: In the presence of an integrin αv blocking antibody, CD cell adhesion to fibronectin was decreased.
source: As these cells express integrin αv, the same experiment was carried out in the presence of an integrin αv blocking antibody. Under these conditions CD cell adhesion was decreased, albeit less than the adhesion defect observed with the CD cells adhering to collagen I or IV.
evidence: This is a finding based on cell adhesion data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: No differences in cell adhesion were seen when the cells adhered to fibronectin in the presence of an anti-β1 antibody.
source: No differences in cell adhesion were seen when the cells adhered to fibronectin in the presence of an anti-β1 antibody, suggesting that the β1-K752E mutation decreased integrin α5β1-dependent adhesion of CD cells to fibronectin.
evidence: This is a finding based on cell adhesion data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The β1-K752E mutation decreased integrin α5β1-dependent adhesion of CD cells to fibronectin.
source: No differences in cell adhesion were seen when the cells adhered to fibronectin in the presence of an anti-β1 antibody, suggesting that the β1-K752E mutation decreased integrin α5β1-dependent adhesion of CD cells to fibronectin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cell adhesion data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: There was decreased intensity of 12G10 in β1K752E CD cells plated on fibronectin, which correlated with the adhesion and spreading defects.
source: Similar to when the cells adhered to collagen I there was decreased intensity of 12 G10 (Figure 8C and D), which correlated with the adhesion and spreading defects.
evidence: This is a finding based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8C and D.

claim: A β1-K752E mutation decreases CD cell adhesion, spreading and integrin α5β1 activation when CD cells bind to fibronectin.
source: Thus a β1-K752E mutation decreases CD cell adhesion, spreading and integrin α5β1 activation when CD cells bind to fibronectin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the collective data in Figure 8.

claim: The talin F3 bound to both β1-WT and β1-K752E TM/CT in POPC/POPS/D6PC bicelles with similar (moderate) affinity (Kd of 27 ± 4 µM and 18 ± 3 µM for WT and K752E β1 TM/CT, respectively).
source: As shown in Figure 9, the talin F3 bound to both β1-WT and β1-K752E TM/CT in POPC/POPS/D6PC bicelles with similar (moderate) affinity (Kd of 27 ± 4 µM and 18 ± 3 µM for WT and K752E β1 TM/CT, respectively).
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR titration data shown in Figure 9.

claim: The β3-K716E mutation results in a 6-fold increase in the Kd for talin-1 binding from 5 ± 2 µM to 30 ± 8 µM.
source: In contrast, the β3-K716E mutation results in a 6-fold increase in the Kd for talin-1 binding from 5 ± 2 µM to 30 ± 8 µM, suggesting the β3-K716E mutation alters the structure and/or dynamics of bicelle-associated β3 TM/CT to reduce talin-1 F3 binding affinity (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR titration data shown in Figure 10.

claim: The β3-K716E mutation alters the structure and/or dynamics of bicelle-associated β3 TM/CT to reduce talin-1 F3 binding affinity.
source: In contrast, the β3-K716E mutation results in a 6-fold increase in the Kd for talin-1 binding from 5 ± 2 µM to 30 ± 8 µM, suggesting the β3-K716E mutation alters the structure and/or dynamics of bicelle-associated β3 TM/CT to reduce talin-1 F3 binding affinity (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the talin binding data shown in Figure 10.

claim: Mutation of the snorkeling lysine of β3, but not of β1, significantly reduces the affinity of the talin F3 domain for the isolated integrin subunit.
source: These results indicate that mutation of the snorkeling lysine of β3, but not of β1, significantly reduces the affinity of the talin F3 domain for the isolated integrin subunit.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the talin binding data in Figures 9 and 10.

claim: The affinity of F3 for both the β1 and β3 TM/CT is higher by over an order of magnitude than the affinity of F3 for the isolated CT of these integrins in buffer minus either membranes or a membrane-mimetic.
source: The affinity of F3 for both the β1 and β3 TM/CT is higher by over an order of magnitude than the affinity of F3 for the isolated CT of these integrins in buffer minus either membranes or a membrane-mimetic (Kd of 490 µM and 270–600 µM for β1 and β3, respectively) (Moore et al., 2012; Saltel et al., 2009; Anthis et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a comparison with prior work, supported by citations.

claim: The full affinity of the complex between talin and the integrin β3 CT in membranes containing an anionic lipid (Kd ca. 0.9 μM) requires the presence of a linked talin F2 domain.
source: On the other hand, it should be acknowledged that the full affinity of the complex between talin and the integrin β3 CT in membranes containing an anionic lipid (Kd ca. 0.9 μM) requires the presence of a linked talin F2 domain (Moore et al., 2012).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: The structures of the β1 and β3 CT/TM in bicelles are distinct.
source: We show that the structures of the β1 and β3 CT/TM in bicelles are distinct.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion based on the NMR structural data in Figure 2.

claim: The highly conserved 'snorkeling lysine' does not play a role in defining the tilt of either β1 or β3.
source: Also, the highly conserved 'snorkeling lysine' that plays a key role in regulating αIIβ3 activation plays an opposite role in β1 integrin function and does not play a role in defining the tilt of either β1 or β3.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion based on the paramagnetic probe accessibility data in Figures 3-5.

claim: Very different affinities exist between β1 and some α subunits relative to those observed between αIIb and β3.
source: Very different affinities exist between β1 and some α subunits relative to those observed between αIIb and β3.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion based on the binding data in Table 1.

claim: The diverse biophysical properties of β1 and β3 integrin TM and CT domains in combination with varying α subunit properties result in distinct mechanisms of integrin activation and function.
source: We therefore conclude that the diverse biophysical properties of β1 and β3 integrin TM and CT domains in combination with varying α subunit properties result in distinct mechanisms of integrin activation and function.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, inferred from the collective experimental data.

claim: In contrast to integrin αIIbβ3 expressed in a CHO cell, the β1-K752E mutation does not promote integrin activation but actually decreases integrin α1β1, α2β1 and α5β1 epithelial cell adhesion to their respective ligands.
source: In this study, we show that, in contrast to integrin αIIbβ3 expressed in a CHO cell, the β1-K752E mutation does not promote integrin activation (Kim et al., 2012) but actually decreases integrin α1β1, α2β1 and α5β1 epithelial cell adhesion to their respective ligands, with little effect on cell spreading.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion based on the cell adhesion and activation data in Figures 1 and 8.

claim: A previous study showed that expression of β1-K752L in integrin β1-null fibroblasts did not alter the integrin activation status or the ability of the cells to adhere to fibronectin and laminin-111.
source: A previous study showed that expression of β1-K752L in integrin β1-null fibroblasts did not alter the integrin activation status or the ability of the cells to adhere to fibronectin and laminin-111; however this mutation did inhibit cell spreading and migration (Armulik et al., 2004).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: The mechanism for the altered integrin β1-K752L-mediated cell function was proposed to be due to altered phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase activation that impacted FAK-independent integrin signaling without altering integrin activation.
source: The mechanism for the altered integrin β1-K752L-mediated cell function was proposed to be due to altered phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase activation that impacted FAK-independent integrin signaling without altering integrin activation (Armulik et al., 2004).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: β3-K716 was previously believed to stabilize the integrin αIIbβ3 inactive state by forming a salt bridge between its amino side chain and anionic phosphodiester linkages in the phospholipid head groups.
source: β3-K716 was previously believed to stabilize the integrin αIIbβ3 inactive state by forming a salt bridge between its amino side chain and anionic phosphodiester linkages in the phospholipid head groups (Kim et al., 2012).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: This interaction has been proposed to be a key determinant of the TM tilt that is required for optimal outer and inner clasp interactions between the αIIb and β3 subunits, which are present only in the inactive state.
source: This interaction has been proposed to be a key determinant of the TM tilt that is required for optimal outer and inner clasp interactions between the αIIb and β3 subunits, which are present only in the inactive state (Kim et al., 2012).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: β1-WT and β1-K752E integrin exhibit the same PRE patterns, indicating that the tilt of the β1 integrin TM is independent of the charge of residue 752.
source: To our surprise, we observed that β1-WT and β1-K752E integrin exhibit the same PRE patterns, indicating that the tilt of the β1 integrin TM is independent of the charge of residue 752.
evidence: This is a finding based on paramagnetic probe accessibility data in Figure 3.

claim: The mechanism by which β3-K716 promotes the inactive signaling state must now again be regarded as unknown.
source: Thus, not only does β1-K752 promote functional output that is opposite to that promoted by β3-K716, but even in the case of β3 the mechanism by which β3-K716 promotes the inactive signaling state must now again be regarded as unknown.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the collective data showing that the snorkeling mechanism does not explain TM tilt.

claim: The results are consistent with another study that used a biotin maleimide chemical modification of engineered Cys side chains to show that the K716P mutation in β3 did not result in any change in membrane topology.
source: Our results are consistent with another study that used a biotin maleimide chemical modification of engineered Cys side chains to show that the K716P mutation in β3 did not result in any change in membrane topology (Kurtz et al., 2012).
evidence: This references prior work that supports the current findings, supported by citation.

claim: The talin F3 domain binds to the WT β3 TM/CT significantly more tightly than to WT β1 TM/CT (Kd for β3 lower by a factor of 5).
source: Consistent with previous work (Anthis et al., 2010), we found that the talin F3 domain binds to the WT β3 TM/CT significantly more tightly than to WT β1 TM/CT (Kd for β3 lower by a factor of 5).
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR titration data in Figures 9 and 10, consistent with prior work cited.

claim: The β3-K716E mutation increased Kd for talin binding by a factor of 6, a finding that does not correlate well with the proposed activation-promoting nature of this mutation.
source: Interestingly, the β3-K716E mutation increased Kd for talin binding by a factor of 6, a finding that that does not correlate well with the proposed activation-promoting nature of this mutation.
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR titration data in Figure 10, with an interpretation about its implications.

claim: The β1-K752E mutation alters Kd by less than 2-fold and does so in favor of tighter binding to talin.
source: On the other hand, the β1-K752E mutation alters Kd by less than 2-fold and does so in favor of tighter binding.
evidence: This is a finding based on NMR titration data in Figure 9.

claim: At face value these results suggest that the impact of the TM K-to-E mutation on talin binding is not the basis for how this mutation alters integrin function.
source: While possible roles for the F0-F2 talin domains in possible coupling between the TM lysine site and talin binding were not tested in this study, at face value these results suggest that the impact of the TM K-to-E mutation on talin binding is not the basis for how this mutation alters integrin function, once again suggesting a mechanism whereby the TM K-to-E mutation alters integrin function by altering integrin-dependent signaling and not activation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the talin binding data.

claim: Talin binds to both integrin TM/CT domains in bicelles more tightly than to CT-only domains in buffer.
source: It is interesting that talin binds to both integrin TM/CT domains in bicelles more tightly than to CT-only domains in buffer (Moore et al., 2012; Anthis et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a comparison with prior work, supported by citations.

claim: Bicelles most likely promote a more native-like conformational state of the CT in the context of its attached and bicelle-anchored TM than for the isolated CT in solution.
source: Bicelles most likely promote a more native-like conformational state of the CT in the context of its attached and bicelle-anchored TM than for the isolated CT in solution.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the talin binding affinity differences.

claim: The β1 TM ends after I758 while the β3 TM ends after I721.
source: The β1 TM ends after I758 while the β3 TM ends after I721, in reasonably good accord with previous NMR, EPR, and biochemical studies.
evidence: This is a finding based on the paramagnetic probe accessibility data in Figure 3, consistent with prior work.

claim: The TM helix of both β1 and β3 was seen to extend into the cytosol and through the juxtamembrane residues that form the inner clasp, albeit with some fraying.
source: The TM helix of both β1 and β3 was seen to extend into the cytosol and through the juxtamembrane residues that form the inner clasp, albeit with some fraying.
evidence: This is a finding based on the NMR structural data in Figure 2.

claim: Unlike β1, where the helix ends with the clasp at K765, the helix in the β3 extends a full 10 residues further into the subunit, ending only at A737.
source: However, unlike β1, where the helix ends with the clasp at K765, the helix in the β3 extends a full 10 residues further into the subunit, ending only at A737 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding based on the NMR structural data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A continuous β3 TM/CT extends to D740 as part of the αIIbβ3 TM/CT heterodimer in an organic solvent mixture.
source: This result is reminiscent of the observations that a continuous β3 TM/CT extends to D740 as part of the αIIbβ3 TM/CT heterodimer in an organic solvent mixture (Yang et al., 2009), while in the corresponding complex for the CT-only heterodimer the β3 helix ends at K738 (Vinogradova et al., 2002).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citations.

claim: A previous cross-linking/computational study of the αIIbβ3 complex in cell membranes indicated the β3 helix extends from the TM far out into the cytosol.
source: A previous cross-linking/computational study of the αIIbβ3 complex in cell membranes also indicated the β3 helix extends from the TM far out into the cytosol (Zhu et al., 2009).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: A previous NMR study of the β3 TM/CT domain in DPC micelles showed an extended CT helix connected to the TM by a flexible linker.
source: Our results are also generally consistent with a previous NMR study of the β3 TM/CT domain in DPC micelles, where an extended CT helix was observed, but was connected to the TM by a flexible linker (Li et al., 2002).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: The combined structural and membrane topological studies offer clear evidence that, on the average, the CT helix for both β1 and β3 TM/CT extends away from the membrane surface into the aqueous phase.
source: The combined structural and membrane topological studies of our work also offer clear evidence that, on the average, the CT helix for both β1 and β3 TM/CT extends away from the membrane surface into the aqueous phase.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the collective structural and paramagnetic probe accessibility data.

claim: The results are not consistent with the notion that the CT has significant membrane surface affinity, as suggested based on a previous NMR study of crosslinked αIIb and β3 CT in DPC micelles.
source: Our results are not consistent with the notion that the CT has significant membrane surface affinity, as suggested based on a previous NMR study of crosslinked αIIb and β3 CT in DPC micelles (Metcalf et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a conclusion that contradicts prior work, supported by citation.

claim: Some of the functional differences between β1 and β3 are linked to the different intrinsic conformational preferences of their CT, which likely impacts their selectivity and affinity in engaging their cytosolic effector proteins.
source: Nevertheless, they do suggest that some of the functional differences between β1 and β3 are linked to the different intrinsic conformational preferences of their CT, which likely impacts their selectivity and affinity in engaging their cytosolic effector proteins.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the structural differences observed.

claim: In an NMR structure of the complex of the β3 CT with the talin F3 domain the helix terminates at amino acid 732.
source: It is interesting to note that while we observed the β3 helix to extend through site A737, in an NMR structure of the complex of the β3 CT with the talin F3 domain the helix terminates at amino acid 732 (Wegener et al., 2007), suggesting destabilization of the C terminal end of the helix by talin.
evidence: This references prior work, supported by citation.

claim: Talin destabilizes the C terminal end of the β3 helix.
source: It is interesting to note that while we observed the β3 helix to extend through site A737, in an NMR structure of the complex of the β3 CT with the talin F3 domain the helix terminates at amino acid 732 (Wegener et al., 2007), suggesting destabilization of the C terminal end of the helix by talin.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on comparison with prior work.

claim: For bicelle-associated β1 the helix was seen to terminate at K765, while in a crystal structure of the β1 CT with the talin F2F3 domains this helix does not terminate till A773.
source: Conversely, for bicelle-associated β1 the helix was seen to terminate at K765, while in a crystal structure of the β1 CT with the talin F2F3 domains this helix does not terminate till A773 (Anthis et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a comparison with prior work, supported by citation.

claim: The end of the β3 TM/CT helix is not very stable but is readily disrupted by events such as engagement by talin.
source: These results suggest that the end of the β3 TM/CT helix is not very stable but is readily disrupted by events such as engagement by talin.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on comparison of the current data with prior structural studies.

claim: The disordered segment C-terminal to the β1 TM/CT helix does have helical propensity that is manifested upon complex formation with talin.
source: At the same time the disordered segment C-terminal to the β1 TM/CT helix does have helical propensity that is manifested upon complex formation with talin.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on comparison of the current data with prior structural studies.

claim: The metastability of secondary structure in both β1 and β3 CT seems well suited to enable optimal interactions to cytosolic binding partners.
source: The metastability of secondary structure in both β1 and β3 CT seems well suited to enable optimal interactions to cytosolic binding partners.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the structural findings.

claim: The interactions of different α subunit TM/CT with the β1 TM/CT are characterized by very different affinities, ranging from very weak interactions between α1 or α2 and β1 to much higher affinity interaction between α5 and β1, similar to that found between αIIb and β3.
source: Finally, the data demonstrated that the interactions of different α subunit TM/CT with the β1 TM/CT are characterized by very different affinities, ranging from very weak interactions between α1 or α2 and β1 to much higher affinity interaction between α5 and β1, similar to that found between αIIb and β3.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion based on the binding data in Table 1.

claim: It has been widely assumed that the TM/CT of β integrins have an intrinsic affinity for the corresponding domains of their cognate α subunits, such that they will form constitutively inactive heterodimers.
source: Based mostly on studies of the αIIbβ3 integrin it has been widely assumed that the TM/CT of β integrins have an intrinsic affinity for the corresponding domains of their cognate α subunits, such that they will form constitutively inactive heterodimers.
evidence: This describes a widely held assumption in the field based on prior work.

claim: Many studies have shown the isolated αIIb and β3 TM associate to form heterodimers in model membranes or as fusion proteins in E. coli or model cell lines.
source: Many studies have shown the isolated αIIb and β3 TM associate to form heterodimers in model membranes or as fusion proteins in E. coli or model cell lines (Lau et al., 2009; Berger et al., 2010; Partridge et al., 2005; Zhu et al., 2010; Schneider and Engelman, 2004; Schmidt et al., 2015; Lokappa et al., 2014; Kim et al., 2009).
evidence: This references prior work, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The observation that α5 and β1 TM/CT form heterodimers is consistent with evidence that this particular β1 integrin is activated according to the canonical model.
source: We observed similar results for heterodimerization of the α5 and β1 TM/CT, an observation consistent with evidence that this particular β1 integrin is activated according to the canonical model (Takagi et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the binding data in Table 1, consistent with prior work cited.

claim: α1 and β1 as well as α2 and β1 TM/CT interactions were too weak to be quantified in bicelles, even at the high protein concentrations required for NMR spectroscopy.
source: In contrast, we found that α1 and β1 as well as α2 and β1 TM/CT interactions were too weak to be quantified in bicelles, even at the high protein concentrations required for NMR spectroscopy.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on the binding data in Table 1.

claim: Studies suggesting that the fusion proteins containing the TM-only domain of α1β1 and α2β1 can form heterodimers in E. coli were conducted in the absence of the β1, α1, and α2 CT, which almost certainly profoundly impact heterodimerization.
source: This is surprising in light of studies suggesting that the fusion proteins containing the TM-only domain of these integrin subunits can form heterodimers in E. coli (Berger et al., 2010; Schneider and Engelman, 2004). However, these latter studies were conducted in the absence of the β1, α1, and α2 CT, which almost certainly profoundly impact heterodimerization (Briesewitz et al., 1995; Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a discussion of prior work and its limitations, supported by citations.

claim: The α1 and α2 CT may actually inhibit formation of α1β1 and α2β1 TM/CT heterodimers, at least in bicelles.
source: Our results suggest that the α1 and α2 CT may actually inhibit formation of α1β1 and α2β1 TM/CT heterodimers, at least in bicelles.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the weak binding observed for α1β1 and α2β1.

claim: The stark contrast between the collagen α1β1 and α2β1 integrins and the fibronectin α5β1 integrin suggests that the role of TM/CT domain heterodimerization in regulating integrin function may vary considerably among different β1 integrins.
source: The stark contrast between the collagen α1β1 and α2β1 integrins and the fibronectin α5β1 integrin suggests that the role of TM/CT domain heterodimerization in regulating integrin function may vary considerably among different β1 integrins, as previously proposed (Nissinen et al., 2012; Abair et al., 2008b; Bazzoni et al., 1998; Pepinsky et al., 2002; Bodeau et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the binding data, consistent with prior proposals cited.

claim: Integrins α1β1 and α2β1 may remain constitutively in their unclasped α/β-TM/CT-dissociated forms.
source: Our results for integrins α1β1 and α2β1 suggest the intriguing possibility that these receptors may remain constitutively in their unclasped α/β-TM/CT-dissociated forms, implying their signaling functions are modulated via mechanisms other than the canonical model of switching between TM/CT-clasped and unclasped forms (Abair et al., 2008a; Nissinen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the weak binding observed for α1β1 and α2β1, consistent with prior proposals cited.

claim: Some integrins may be constitutively active or unclasped has long been postulated.
source: That some integrins may be constitutively active or unclasped has long been postulated (Bazzoni and Hemler, 1998).
evidence: This references prior speculation in the field, supported by citation.

claim: The energetics of heterodimerization of isolated TM/CT will not be the same as local TM/CT heterodimerization in the context of full length integrin subunits.
source: However, even considering that the energetics of heterodimerization of isolated TM/CT will not be the same as local TM/CT heterodimerization in the context of full length integrin subunits, these results indicate that the energetics of TM/CT heterodimerization vary dramatically from integrin to integrin.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of the study, followed by a conclusion.

claim: The energetics of TM/CT heterodimerization vary dramatically from integrin to integrin.
source: However, even considering that the energetics of heterodimerization of isolated TM/CT will not be the same as local TM/CT heterodimerization in the context of full length integrin subunits, these results indicate that the energetics of TM/CT heterodimerization vary dramatically from integrin to integrin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the binding data in Table 1.

claim: While integrin αIIbβ3 is found in both active and inactive conformations, a subclass of β1 integrins (α1β1 and α2β1) may adopt a constitutively active conformation.
source: In conclusion, we present evidence that while integrin αIIbβ3 is found in both active and inactive conformations, a subclass of β1 integrins (α1β1 and α2β1) may adopt a constitutively active conformation.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the collective data.

claim: β1 and β3 integrins appear to have distinct mechanisms of action wherein different modes of integrin regulation likely occur within the β1 integrin class based on which α subunit is involved, as well as which cell type.
source: Thus β1 and β3 integrins appear to have distinct mechanisms of action wherein different modes of integrin regulation likely occur within the β1 integrin class based on which α subunit is involved, as well as which cell type.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the collective data.
